name: Codit: Batch Operations
description: Provides methods and framework for running batch operations.
project_description: Codit: Batch Operations is a developer framework for defining and running batch jobs against Drupal content. A batch job is a PHP class (a "BatchOperation script") that implements BatchScriptInterface: it gathers a set of items, processes them one at a time, and records the whole run into a BatchOpLog entity. The same script can be invoked from hook_update_N(), hook_post_update_NAME(), Drush deploy hooks, cron, the Drush command drush codit-batch-operations:run, or an optional web UI (the codit_batch_operations_ui submodule). Runs are resumable: if a run is interrupted by an error, exception, timeout, or the operator navigating away, state is stored so the next invocation picks up where it left off, and every step is written to a per-run log entity for auditing. Scripts can stop on the first error or gracefully skip failing items and continue. A configurable default user is attributed to entity saves, and helper traits provide common node- and taxonomy-term operations. The module ships example/test scripts and a StarterScript template. Because a script is arbitrary code that mutates content at scale, the UI-run and administer permissions are marked restrict access.
